title: Finch: A Great App I Wouldn’t Recommend
body:
I was enamored by the concept. I have a 137-day streak ongoing. At first, it helped with reminding me of small self-care tasks, like drinking water, eating on time, getting out of bed—stuff like that. But I’m better at those things now; they’ve become almost natural to me. I no longer need a digital reward to keep at it; the benefits of self-care is a reward, in and of itself. 

Keeping streaks with friends, getting rewards everyday through events, keeping a daily streak, earning gems for the items you like—I feel like all those distract from real productivity and end up being unnecessary clutter and mental load. I feel like it can make someone do the right things for the wrong reason. I feel like it does a lot of things to keep you using the app.

I was caught up in it for a bit, but I have figured out a healthier and calmer way of taking care of myself and hitting productivity milestones, without relying on micro-hits of dopamine.

For the help it gave me when I was getting out of a hard place (and I give kudos to the developers for creating a genuinely cute app), I’ll give it grace and rate it a 4/5, but would I recommend this app moving forward? No. There are simpler, better, healthier ways to achieve self-care in my opinion.

title: You won’t feel pressured with Finch
body:
I have used the Free trial and the free version and both are extremely good! With the free version, you literally get everything that you need. The app developers are not stingy about the meditation needs that people in emergency situations might need. 

Unlike other apps, I never feel pressured with Finch. I feel that I want to be better and take care of my little birb, which takes care of myself as well. 

You know, I have a feeling the app developers read through Atomic Habits and realized that 1% of good habits every day comes a long way because as I was doing the guided habits, I feel a lot better with the little activities I’m doing everyday. 

I hope my little birdie grows in the future just like her owner. 😊 See you all in Finch.

title: Hi! This is a great app!
body:
I’ve had Finch for a few weeks now and I’ve got to say it’s been helpful and good for me. I usually don’t like these kinds of apps because I find them kind of “fake” or hard to trust in/confide to, but Finch asks questions that help me organize my thoughts and reach my goals for the day. If not for myself, then at least for my little finch and for rainbow stones. 

One of my suggestions is that maybe we could get more choices and adventures for our finches? I think that would make the app more interactive. I also hope we get more questions for daily things, and not just the same old questions (even though they still help).
